notes:
- A relation opens the whole page, not a slice of it: Tapping a related title inside a page opened a visibly emptier page than the same title opened from the list: "no synopsis available", no credits, no studios, and the relations row gone after a single hop. The sheet did fetch the full record - the page was handed the thin relation node the card carried, so the answer was thrown away. A relation now resolves through the fetched detail exactly the way an arriving row already did, and keeps the progress from the entry you tapped.
- The progress wave stops redrawing the page it sits on: The wavy progress bar read its animation state during composition, so every frame of the wave recomposed the page around it, and its fill started from zero again whenever the row came back into view or you followed a relation to another title. The wave is drawn in the draw phase now, a bar with nothing to show composes no animation at all, and the fill slides to the new value across a hop instead of replaying its entrance.
- Your list is still there when you reopen the app: The list, your own profile and every title page were held in memory only, so closing the app threw all of it away and the next launch bought the whole list back from AniList - a request per chunk of it - before it could draw a single row. All of it is now snapshotted under the cache directory, so a launch inside its window spends nothing. Signing out deletes all of it.
- A title's synopsis, cast and studios are remembered for a day: Opening a title re-fetched its whole record on every launch, even one already read through a minute earlier. That record - synopsis, cast, staff, studios, release year, relations - is now reused for 24 hours, so the page opens full and instantly; what genuinely moves inside it, like the score or the next airing episode, is asked for again the next day.
- Your own profile is re-fetched at most every half hour: Every launch began with a request no screen had asked for: the viewer's own profile, needed before the dashboard could name the account or ask for a list. It is now reused for thirty minutes. A pasted token is still checked against AniList first - the caches are cleared before that check, so a stored profile can never vouch for a session AniList has refused.
- Your own comments can now be edited or deleted: A comment could be written and liked, and that was the end of it: a typo was permanent and a comment you no longer stood behind stayed in somebody else's thread. Your own comments now carry an options menu that leads to an editor - seeded with the text on screen - and to a delete behind a confirmation. Both go through AniList, so the thread everyone reads is the one you changed, and a delete moves the activity's comment count with it. Only your own comments get the menu; drawing it on anybody else's would be inviting a tap the server refuses.
- The comment box enforces AniList's own limits: AniList refuses a comment shorter than two characters, and the sheet used to send it anyway and print the server's refusal as a failure - a lone letter or emoji was a round trip that could only end badly. The send button now waits for a second character and says why, the field stops accepting text at the eight thousand the schema allows rather than letting you write a comment that will bounce, and the keyboard's Send action posts exactly the way the button does.
- Waiting screens are drawn as the screen that is coming: The activity feed, a comment thread, the likers sheet and the Social tab answered every load with a spinner in the middle of an otherwise empty page, then replaced it with the full layout. Each now draws a shimmering sketch of the rows it is about to show - the card, the comment, the face - at the sizes those rows actually have, so the data lands into a layout you were already looking at instead of replacing one.
- A failed likers list offers a way back: The sheet that answers who liked an activity printed its failure as a sentence with no way forward, unlike the comment thread, whose failure offers the request one tap away. The same failure now carries the same Try again button.
